claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The narrative identifies the evidence as the 'fact that he gave a speech,' which constitutes conduct or an event rather than an out-of-court 'statement' as required by FRE 801(a).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) defines a 'statement' as oral or written words or nonverbal conduct of a declarant if the declarant intended it as an assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that he gave a speech there in 2005

arguments.text: The act of giving a speech is non-assertive conduct; it does not rely on the declarant's intent to assert that he visited Chicago, failing the assertion prong of the hearsay definition.
arguments.legal_rule: Under FRE 801(a), nonverbal conduct is only a 'statement' if the declarant intended it as an assertion. Mere conduct without assertive intent is not hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that he gave a speech there in 2005

arguments.text: The evidence is offered to prove Richard visited Chicago through circumstantial implication of the act, not to prove the truth of any asserted matter, which excludes it from FRE 801(c).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) excludes evidence offered to prove a fact through circumstantial implication rather than the truth of an asserted proposition.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Richard had ever visited Chicago
